A developer keeps one Claude Code session open all week. Monday it fixes a token refresh bug, Tuesday it builds a CSV export, Wednesday it chases a flaky test. Auto-compaction has run twice, and they've typed

a few more times "to keep it fresh". On Wednesday afternoon, Claude calls the legacy HTTP client that, back on Monday, they'd told it never to use. That instruction lived only in the conversation, and the conversation is now a summary of a summary.

items.text: Compaction is automatic. Claude Code compacts as you approach the limit, so a full context window never ends the session, and it feels lossless.
The summary is good. The docs say it keeps your requests and key code snippets.
Context windows are large. With a 1M-token window on most current models, the docs themselves say running out is rare.
Starting over feels like throwing away what Claude "learned" about the code.

content.text: The half-truth: compaction does preserve a lot, and some things reload from disk afterward. But it's a summary, not a save point. It loses detail by design, and it doesn't separate Monday's task from Wednesday's.
replaces the conversation history with a structured summary. Then Claude Code rebuilds part of the context:

items.text: The system prompt and output style still apply.
The project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules and auto memory are re-injected from disk.
A plan written in plan mode is re-injected from disk.
Up to five files Claude read or edited are re-read, most recently modified first; a file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path reference without its content.
Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md files reload only when Claude touches a matching file again.

content.text: The conversation itself, including every instruction you gave in chat, now exists only as the summary's version of it. The docs warn that detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost.

The model remembers nothing between requests, so Claude Code re-sends the full context on every turn. With prompt caching, that history is re-read at the cached rate, but the costs page is blunt: "a one-line question in a session that has been open all day still draws usage for the whole conversation." The context-window guide adds that old conversation crowds out the files you need next.
To write the summary, Claude Code sends a request that reads the history being summarized. While the
is warm, that prefix comes from the cache and the request costs a fraction of its size. After a break longer than the cache lifetime, the same history is reprocessed as uncached input.

A rewind truncates the conversation back to a prefix that's already cached, while compaction has to build a new one. To abandon a path, rewind instead of compacting over it.

A rule you only typed in the conversation, like "never use the legacy client", can disappear in a compaction. Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md, which is re-injected from disk. To steer every compaction, add a "Compact Instructions" section there, such as "keep failing test names and API decisions".
